name: Missouri
standard: Missouri State ICT Standard 3.0 — WCAG 2.2 A/AA (from 2026-04-06; WCAG 2.1 before) + Section 508

laws.summary: State departments and agencies of all three branches, incl. public colleges, must make IT they develop, procure, maintain or use accessible unless an undue burden; MoAT and ITSD adopt standards, review procedures and complaint procedures.

laws.cite: 28 CFR Part 35, Subpart H (ADA Title II web & mobile rule, 2024; dates extended by IFR 2026-07663)
laws.summary: Federal floor: state and local government web content and mobile apps must conform to WCAG 2.1 AA; the April 2026 IFR moved compliance to 2027-04-26 (pop. 50,000+) and 2028-04-26 (smaller entities and special districts).

policy_docs.title: MoAT — ICT Laws & Standards (Missouri State ICT Standard 3.0)

applies_to: Each department, office, board, bureau, commission or unit of the executive, legislative or judicial branch, incl. public 2- and 4-year colleges; contracts and grants that include IT.

deadlines.what: Roadmap: designate agency Digital Accessibility Coordinator
WCAG 2.2 A/AA compliance deadline under ICT Standard 3.0
Roadmap final deadline (agency Digital Accessibility Plan follow-up)
ADA Title II rule: state government and local governments with population 50,000+ must conform web content and mobile apps to WCAG 2.1 AA (extended from 2026-04-24 by DOJ IFR effective 2026-04-20)
ADA Title II rule: local governments under 50,000 and special district governments (extended from 2027-04-26)

requires: Agency Digital Accessibility Coordinator; training within 90 days
Inventory/audit of websites, apps, mobile apps and documents
Review of custom systems before spending state funds
mobile: explicit — ICT Standard scope and procurement language list mobile applications; roadmap inventories mobile apps.
procurement: All IT solicitations must require a VPAT (ACR); contractors must assure conformance to the Missouri State ICT Standard and describe testing methods; suggested contract language provided.
enforcement: MoAT/ITSD complaint procedures under RSMo §161.935(3)(6); undue-burden exception; ADA Title II. Contact digital.accessibility@oa.mo.gov.
notes: MoAT page and roadmap disagree on WCAG 2.1 effective dating (roadmap: WCAG 2.1 effective 2025-03-13, WCAG 2.2 effective 2026-04-06; MoAT page: WCAG 2.2 effective 2025-10-05 with 6-month compliance to 2026-04-06). ICT Standard 3.0 approved 2024-09-13; the standard PDF itself was not opened. Roadmap uses pre-extension 2026-04-24 date.
